original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove the exact joint ordered-subproduct cover criterion for diagonal targets over any field and group, with arbitrary finite scalar workspace, fixed free scalar maps and unit-cost idempotent group gates of arbitrary rank. Apply it to the order-21 target and classify all distinct nonidentity triples in C7, C7 semidirect C3 and Q8.
scope_change_reason: The rank-one finite model is enlarged to arbitrary fields, finite scalar workspace, singular free maps and arbitrary-rank unit gates. The old target minimum is credited; the new question is whether these resources permit a two-call escape and whether a simultaneous support cover is sufficient.
bottleneck_link: The actual order-21 three-call floor survives this larger class. Its formal obstruction screens a workspace-sharing route before a physical compiler search. Positive relaxed constructions are not physical savings.
stop_rule: Finish the quantified support-cover proof, full independent triple classifications, exact constructions and scope controls. Do not expand the group census or claim a physical supplier.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the all-field/all-group theorem. Two implementations agree on 1195 triples and verify 121800 regular-action columns including dirty returns. The primary checks 216 full-cover constructions, 96 scalar interleavings and 12 controls. The coefficient-cut proof gives rank at least two in each gate of any two-call triple realization; 96 finite scalar-map cases check both identities. Thus every distinct nonidentity triple has exact rank-one and rank-charged minimum three in the unrestricted group alphabet.
author: Ali Romman
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with proof, exact replay, source checks, controls and documentation. Both implementations are same-session work, not independent human review.

open_questions.question: When does rank-one cost exceed cover cost for four or more distinct targets with arbitrary finite scalar workspace?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact two-call rank cut does not handle collisions in longer ordered subproducts.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one group and target, then prove coefficient cuts that survive subproduct collisions before a larger search.
open_questions.blocked_by: The two-call proof uses four distinct labels. No general longer-word invariant or physical supplier tariff is given.
